items.label: camera in the description
items.note: Describe what is on screen; the reader is not the camera.

items.label: camera direction
items.note: A spec script leaves shots to the director; write the image, not the lens.

items.label: intensifier
items.note: If it is sudden, the sentence can be.

items.label: weak verb phrase
items.note: She cries, not begins to cry.

items.label: unfilmable description
items.note: Show it as an action or cut it; the camera cannot see a thought.

items.label: stock reaction
items.note: Describe the face or the choice.

items.label: stock gesture
items.note: A stalling beat; replace it with an action.

items.label: stock reaction
items.note: Show the surprise in what the character does.

items.label: stock reaction
items.note: Name what the body does that this scene alone would cause.
items.negative: The heart of the town is its clock.

items.label: stock reaction
items.note: Let the audience supply the tear.
items.positive: A tear rolls down her cheek.

items.label: stock opening
items.note: Waking up is the most common first scene there is.

items.label: stock device
items.note: Introducing a character through a mirror is a well-known shortcut.

items.label: expository dialogue
items.note: Characters do not tell each other what both know.
items.positive: As you know, the gate closes at dusk.

items.label: stock line
items.note: Start the conversation; do not announce it.

items.label: stock line
items.note: The quiet-before-the-storm line is a cliché.

items.label: on-the-nose dialogue
items.note: Give the feeling an action or a subtext.

items.label: stalling parenthetical
items.note: Write the pause into the action or the rhythm of the line.
